Subject: Deployment pathway & GPU fit — recap and asks (Optivex pilot)

Hi Sam —

Great to meet yesterday. Quick written recap and concrete asks so we can size a Dedicated path vs Hosted/Private for your pilot. Short summary of what I captured from the call: 

- Objective: 90-day pilot (customer-facing) to validate semantic search + conversational flows for Optivex support product.
- Target steady throughput: ~150 requests/sec (sustained).
- Burst window: short bursts up to ~600–800 rps (marketing events / peak hours).
- Average token mix: prompts ~80 tokens, responses ~350 tokens (avg).
- Latency target: P95 <= 400 ms for conversation responses.
- Data requirements: some customer PII; you indicated preference for data isolation and audit logs.

High-level guidance we covered: Hosted API is fastest to get started but may add variability during large bursts; Dedicated Reserved pool gives predictable throughput and isolation (better for your SLA needs); Private VPC/on‑prem is an option if you need full network isolation/audit controls.

What we need from you to finalize sizing and a recommended deployment mode: 
1) Traffic trace (1–3 days) showing timestamps, request sizes, and token counts — this lets us model token/sec and KV cache hit patterns.
2) Confirmation of acceptable P95 latency target and max allowed cold-starts.
3) Any regulatory constraints that mandate VPC/on‑prem.

Attachments: optivex_capacity_worksheet.xlsx (filled outline for TPS, token mix, business hours, burst windows).

Next steps I propose:
- Please upload a small traffic sample and the answers above into the Drive link I shared (or reply with attachment).
- I'll loop in Karthik for a short technical sizing session (30–45m) to go through GPU tradeoffs (H100 vs A100), batching, and autoscale behavior.
- Targeting a technical call next week (I can do Tue/Wed morning PST).

Thanks — looking forward to the data so we can give a concrete node count and a cost/latency tradeoff.

- Token mix: prompt ~75–90 tokens (varies by flow), response target average 320–380 tokens.
- Typical session concurrency: ~20–30 concurrent active user sessions for the pilot; we expect bursts driven by scheduled notifications and email campaigns.

Subject: Re: Deployment pathway & GPU fit — quick sizing heuristics

Hi Sam — looping in with a quick technical take based on the worksheet and the sample trace you uploaded. Below are rough back-of-envelope numbers; we should validate with a short benchmark run but this will let us narrow options.

Key inputs (from your sheet/sample):
- Avg tokens per request: prompt 80 + response 350 = ~430 tokens
- Steady TPS (requests/sec): 150 (sustained)
- Burst peak: 800 rps for short windows

Derived load: tokens/sec = TPS * avg_tokens = 150 * 430 ≈ 64,500 tokens/sec sustained.

Sizing heuristics (model: llama-variant / ~30B params; throughput numbers approximate):
- H100 (dense): higher single‑request throughput and lower P95 latency; good for low-latency SLOs. For your profile, expect ~40–60 rps per GPU at P95 < 300ms for ~350-token responses depending on batching and kernel choices.
- A100 80GB (dense/quantized): cheaper per-hour; with aggressive batching you can push more tokens/sec but P95 latency increases. Expect ~20–35 rps per GPU at similar config if prioritizing cost.

Recommendation for Dedicated baseline (steady 150 rps + headroom + typical autoscale):
- H100 path: start with 4 x H100s in a reserved pool -> provides steady capacity and room to absorb load variance; autoscale additional burst nodes up to 8 H100s for short spikes.
- A100 path: start with 8 x A100s reserved -> would meet steady needs but require more instances for bursts (autoscale to ~16 A100s).

Notes on caching & autoscale:
- Prefix/KV cache: a high KV hit-rate can reduce effective tokens/sec dramatically for conversational flows with repeated context; we should instrument for that.
- Autoscaling: for burst scenarios we recommend a mix of reserved baseline + burst pool enabled (reserve spot capacity for bursts).

Next actions I propose:
1) Run a 4‑hour bench with your sample payload against both an H100 and an A100 node image (we can stage this in our test cluster). I expect the test to show the H100 P95 advantage on 350-token outputs.
2) We'll return a recommended node count and an estimate for monthly reserved cost vs pay-as-you-go (hosted).

If you can confirm a 60–90 minute slot Tue or Wed next week, I can run through the bench plan and expected metrics.

Cheers,
